items.title: The separation axioms for a morphism of formal algebraic spaces can be checked on affine base changes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of formal algebraic spaces and any of the separation axioms, the lemma states the equivalence of five formulations: the axiom itself; the axiom after base change to every scheme; after base change to every affine scheme; the statement that the affine base changes are of the corresponding type as formal algebraic spaces; and the axiom for the members of one presentation (statement lines 6884-6911). The first two implications are immediate once the stability of the axiom under base change is granted. The proof then supplies three genuinely different arguments. It passes from the third to the fourth by computing the relevant fibre product as a base change of the product of two affine schemes along the diagonal, and reading off that the result is quasi-compact, respectively an affine scheme with a closed immersion into that product (proof lines 6915-6926). It passes back from the fourth to the third by reading that computation backwards, using that the fibre products of an etale covering by affines form an etale covering of the square, to conclude the corresponding property for the diagonal (proof lines 6928-6950). The passage from the third to the fifth uses the presentation of the target, writes each member as a filtered colimit of affine formal subschemes, notes that the diagonal for the member is the colimit of the diagonals for the pieces, and concludes by testing after base change along affine schemes into the square, which is exactly what the factorisation statement for such colimits allows (proof lines 6952-6972). The final implication produces a fibre product square for the coproduct of the members of the presentation and uses the descent statement for representable transformations to transfer the property from the left vertical arrow to the right one (proof lines 6974-6981). The claim is H3: four implications are proved by four independent mechanisms -- a fibre product computation with the diagonal, its converse through an etale cover of the square, a colimit argument over a presentation, and a descent along a covering -- and each is displayed.
